candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Rewrite operands into equivalent compatible forms before subtraction, including common-denominator fractions, whole numbers or fractions expressed as mixed-number forms, and normalized mixed numbers.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: A split preparation into unlike-denominator alignment and general number-form standardization, while C combined both into one preparation skill. B clearly identified the common-denominator preparation component in S01; its mixed-number form preparation is partly bundled elsewhere, but S01 aligns directly with the shared preparation concept.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Subtract aligned fractional and whole-number components by subtracting numerators over a shared denominator and subtracting corresponding whole-number parts when using mixed numbers.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: A and C describe the same component-wise subtraction skill, covering both like-denominator numerator subtraction and whole-number subtraction in mixed numbers. B split this across fractional subtraction in S02 and mixed-number structural work, including whole-part subtraction and recombination, in S03.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Adjust and express the result in valid final form by borrowing when a fractional difference is negative, reducing fractions, removing zero parts, and combining whole and fractional components.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: A bundled regrouping and final-answer formatting in one skill. C split this into borrowing/regrouping and final simplification. B explicitly identified the borrowing component in S04, while some final-formatting behavior is bundled into its subtraction and mixed-number structure skills; S04 is the direct alignment for the post-subtraction adjustment portion.

alignment_summary: The three codebooks largely agree on a three-stage structure: prepare operands into compatible forms, subtract aligned components, and then regroup or finalize the answer. The main differences are granularity and bundling: A combines regrouping with finalization, C separates those two, and B distributes mixed-number structure and some final formatting across multiple skills.
